target_parameter: ITT Intervention Effect (HV vs Control, Digital vs Control, HV vs Digital)
key_assumptions: Assumes Missing Completely at Random (MCAR) or that outcome missingness is conditionally independent of unobserved outcomes given model covariates: Y_miss _|_ Y | (T, X).
data_support_in_niyati: Empirically refutable and violated: Outcome missingness differs sharply across randomized arms (6.31% in HV vs 15.84% in Digital, p < 0.001) and is significantly associated with baseline mother age (p < 0.0001), low birth weight (p = 0.028), and household adults (p = 0.018).
methodological_strengths: Simple, transparent, replicates published paper sample (N=2,149). Unbiased under strict MCAR or if missingness depends exclusively on fully observed treatment arms and exogenous predictors.
methodological_vulnerabilities: Discards 312 participants (12.68% of enrolled sample). Severe risk of selection bias if attrited children in the Digital or Control arms had systematically different developmental trajectories. Cannot account for informative non-response, refusal, or mortality.
recommendation_for_niyati: Retain as primary replication benchmark only; do NOT rely on complete-case analysis as the sole evidence base without mandatory missing-data sensitivity analyses.

strategy_name: Multiple Imputation for Primary Outcome (under MAR)
target_parameter: Full-Cohort ITT Intervention Effect (N=2,461 Enrolled Cohort)
key_assumptions: Assumes Missing at Random (MAR): Probability of missing outcome depends strictly on observed baseline covariates and randomized treatment arms: P(R=1 | Y, X, T) = P(R=1 | X, T). Assumes correct conditional imputation model specification.
data_support_in_niyati: Strong observed predictor base: 71.5% of outcome attriters have completely observed baseline profiles (CREDI developmental score, child age, maternal age, birth weight, SES quintile, province, cluster). An additional 20.8% are missing only father variables or MICS activities.
methodological_strengths: Recovers full randomized sample (N=2,461). Preserves intention-to-treat principle. Propagates imputation uncertainty via Rubin's rules. Incorporates cluster structure and rich baseline predictors.
methodological_vulnerabilities: MAR is inherently unprovable from observed data. In V3 baseline imputation, continuous models suffered diagnostic support violations (e.g. 100% invalid integer draws for bl_hhadults). Truncation by death (10 children) violates standard missingness paradigms. Cannot resolve informative dropout.
recommendation_for_niyati: Feasible and recommended as the primary full-cohort sensitivity analysis, provided that: (a) imputation models respect bounded supports; (b) clustering is accounted for; and (c) child deaths are treated separately.

target_parameter: Weighted Average Treatment Effect (Re-weighted to Enrolled Cohort)
key_assumptions: Assumes Selection on Observables / MAR and Positivity: P(R=1 | X, T) > 0 for all X, T. Assumes correct propensity model specification for probability of endline outcome observation.
data_support_in_niyati: Empirically well-supported: Positivity holds across all populated clusters (min cluster follow-up rate = 25.0%, mean = 87.9%). Selection model can leverage arm assignment, mother age, birth weight, and SES.
methodological_strengths: Does not require specifying conditional outcome distribution for non-responders. Re-weights complete cases (N=2,149) to represent the initial randomized baseline population.
methodological_vulnerabilities: Potential variance inflation if weights are extreme (though positivity check indicates bounded weights). Does not address MNAR or outcomes truncated by death. Sensitive to propensity model misspecification.
recommendation_for_niyati: Feasible secondary sensitivity check to evaluate whether re-weighting complete cases alters effect estimates relative to unweighted complete-case analysis.

target_parameter: Robustness Boundary for Treatment Effect under Informative Attrition
key_assumptions: Assumes Missing Not at Random (MNAR): Unobserved outcomes systematically differ from MAR predictions by an offset parameter delta: E[Y_miss | X, T] = E[Y_obs | X, T] + delta_T. Systematically varies delta across plausible ranges to identify tipping points.
data_support_in_niyati: Substantively compelling: 65 families explicitly refused endline assessment, 103 could not be reached after 4+ visits, and Digital attrition was 2.5x higher than Home Visits. Attrited children in Digital may have experienced lower engagement or slower developmental progress.
methodological_strengths: Does not assume benign missingness. Transparently reveals the exact magnitude of unobserved disadvantage (delta) among attriters required to overturn conclusions of active intervention efficacy or equivalence.
methodological_vulnerabilities: Requires subject-matter justification for plausible delta bounds. Generates a sensitivity continuum rather than a single point estimate.
recommendation_for_niyati: Highly recommended as the definitive stress-test for Niyati. A tipping-point grid varying delta from -0.30 SD to +0.10 SD across arms will rigorously establish whether differential attrition undermines the primary trial findings.
